title: The integral derived pullback agrees with the strict-tower completed pullback
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $W\in\{T,T'\}$ let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_W$ be the completed coefficient sheaf on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ the derived category of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]; these are the completed sheaves $A_W$ and the categories $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ of the adic datum $(A,I)=(\mathcal O_E,(\varpi_E))$, $P_n=A_{E,n}$, of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $Lg^*$ be the integral derived pullback of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] and $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ the strict-tower completed pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

Let $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete]. Then $K$ is derived $(\varpi_E)$-complete in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], so $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ is defined, and there is an isomorphism
$$\gamma_{g,K}:Lg^*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K\quad\text{in }D(T'_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E),$$
natural in $K$ and compatible with the $\mathcal O_E$-linear structures, such that for every $n\geq1$ the composite of the defining derived-limit projection $Lg^*K\to\operatorname{Res}_ng^*(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] with the inverse of $\gamma_{g,K}$ is the projection $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K\to\operatorname{Res}_nLg_n^*K_n$ of the defining derived limit of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], where $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ and both finite pullbacks are the exact finite-coefficient module pullback [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, $\gamma_{g,K[r]}$ and $\gamma_{g,K}[r]$ correspond under the termwise shift identification $Lg^*(K[r])=(Lg^*K)[r]$ on K-flat representatives and the shift isomorphism of $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ of [lem-cbc-completed-pullback-triangles].

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$, $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $S_{W,n}=(A/t^n)_W$. The coefficient DVR lemma gives that $A$ is a PID, hence Noetherian, $t\ne0$, and its residue field is finite. The finite-quotient lemma gives that every $A/t^n$ is finite with surjective quotient transitions; in particular $A/(t)$ is additive torsion. The two-term free resolution $[A\xrightarrow{t^n}A]\to A/t^n$, in degrees $[-1,0]$, is exact except at degree zero: multiplication is injective since $A$ is a subring of the field $E$, and its cokernel is the quotient. Thus each quotient is perfect. These verify every coefficient hypothesis of the adic datum in the statement. No finiteness hypothesis on either scheme is required.

source.place: Tag 099L, section-derived-completion-noetherian, coefficient hypotheses; elementary two-term resolution over the coefficient DVR.

proof.text: On each of the two sites, sheafify the constant-presheaf exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{t^n}A\to A/t^n\to0$. Exact abelian sheafification gives the same exact sequence of constant sheaves. The constant/completed coefficient lemma says that $R_W$ is flat over $\underline A_W$ and that $R_W/t^nR_W\cong S_{W,n}$ through the specified projection. Tensoring the constant-sheaf sequence with $R_W$ is exact by the meaning of flatness, so $0\to R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W\to S_{W,n}\to0$ is exact. In particular the augmentation $Q_{W,n}=[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]\to S_{W,n}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Its transitions are multiplication by $t$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree zero; the augmentations commute strictly with the quotient transitions.

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat; apply to the powers of the principal ideal, with the canonical finite quotients.

proof.text: We first justify the domain of the completed functor, without replacing the imported Roos completeness condition by a stronger hypothesis. Apply the finite-free completed scalar comparison with $L=E$. Since $K$ is derived complete in exactly the imported sense, it says that the specified quotient-cone completion map $K\to\mathsf C(K_\bullet)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $K$, with zero shifted-product component on one K-flat representative. Countable products of $R_T$-modules are exact on the pro-etale site. The normalized strict Roos comparison $\rho:\mathsf C(K_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim K_\bullet$ identifies that zero-component map with the strict quotient augmentation's canonical map $\operatorname{comp}_K$. Consequently $\operatorname{comp}_K$ is invertible. This uses the actual completion map, not an arbitrary isomorphism between two objects satisfying Roos triangles.

proof.text: By Koszul reconstruction, $c_K:K^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim K_\bullet$ satisfies $c_K\kappa_K=\operatorname{comp}_K$. Hence $\kappa_K$ is invertible by Step 3. Here the reconstruction's Koszul limit and the intrinsic definition's explicit fiber model have the same canonical unit: on a representative $C$, their common strict tower is $C\otimes Q_{T,m}$, and its degree-zero inclusions give a strict augmentation. The intrinsic coordinates have differential $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$; the cone coordinates have differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$. The map $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$ is a chain isomorphism, and sends the intrinsic unit $(u_C,0)$ to the zero-shifted-component cone unit $(0,u_C)$. The strict Roos comparison identifies this unit with $\kappa_K$. Thus the intrinsic unit is invertible and $K$ is derived $(t)$-complete as claimed.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$. Put $P_n=P\otimes_{R_T}S_{T,n}$ and $X_n=P\otimes_{R_T}Q_{T,n}$, with the strict transitions of Step 2. By the adic-datum construction, $P_\bullet$ represents the entire strict reduction tower $K_\bullet$. The maps $a_n:X_n\to P_n$ are a strict tower quasi-isomorphism: $P$ is K-flat and the augmentation of Step 2 is a quasi-isomorphism. Explicitly, its cone is acyclic; tensoring that cone with $P$ stays acyclic by the definition of K-flatness, and the tensor-cone identity identifies it with the cone of $a_n$. Each $X_n$ is K-flat with flat terms: for an acyclic $N$, $N\otimes X_n$ is, up to the standard tensor-cone signs, the cone of $t^n$ on the acyclic $N\otimes P$, hence acyclic; its terms are finite sums of terms of $P$. Thus $X_\bullet\to P_\bullet$ is an objectwise K-flat replacement of the strict diagram, rather than unrelated choices at each level.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; apply the explicit principal Koszul resolution and the definition of K-flatness.

proof.text: Write $G$ for ordinary module pullback along $c_g:g^{-1}R_T\to R_{T'}$; this notation does not mean the integral completed operation. The resolving-class description of the strict tower pullback computes $V K_\bullet:=Lg^*_{\mathrm{Tow}}K_\bullet$ by $G X_\bullet$, using Step 5. The ringed-topos K-flat pullback lemma applies to the given morphism of small pro-etale topoi and $c_g$; hence $P'=GP$ is K-flat with flat terms over $R_{T'}$. Additivity and scalar linearity identify $GX_n$ with $P'\otimes Q_{T',n}$, including the transition $(t,1)$. Step 2 on $T'$ and K-flatness of $P'$ therefore give a strict tower quasi-isomorphism $GX_\bullet\to(P'\otimes S_{T',n})_n$. This argument never assumes that $c_g$ is an isomorphism or that completed-ring module pullback is exact.

source.place: Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; strict-diagram K-flat computation specified by def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback.

proof.text: Let $B_\bullet=(\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*P_n)_n$ with its actual finite quotient transitions. There is a natural chain isomorphism $P'\otimes_{R_{T'}}S_{T',n}\cong\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*P_n$: both are $g^{-1}P\otimes_{g^{-1}R_T}S_{T',n}$. On the left this is tensor reassociation; on the right use $g^{-1}S_{T,n}\cong S_{T',n}$ and the module tensor construction. The scalar map on both sides is $g^{-1}R_T\to g^{-1}S_{T,n}\to S_{T',n}$, precisely the $n$-th component of $c_g$. The reassociation sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes\bar b a$, with inverse $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. These formulas commute with differentials and with each quotient map $S_{n+1}\to S_n$. Consequently Step 6 supplies a natural isomorphism $b_K:VK_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}B_\bullet$ in the derived category of strict $R_{T'}$-module towers. Finite pullback is exact by the constant-coefficient exactness proposition, so the evaluations of $B_\bullet$ represent the specified finite derived pullbacks.

proof.text:
By the integral-operation definition, the left-hand functor of the item is represented by $\mathsf C(B_\bullet)$. By the completed-pullback definition and Step 4 the right-hand functor is $R\lim(VK_\bullet)$. Define
$$\gamma_{g,K}=\bigl(R\lim(b_K)\bigr)^{-1}\circ\rho_{B_\bullet}:\mathsf C(B_\bullet)\longrightarrow R\lim(VK_\bullet).$$
Both factors are isomorphisms: $b_K$ is the strict-tower isomorphism of Step 7, and $\rho$ is the normalized strict Roos comparison, whose exact-products hypothesis holds on $T'$. Total derived inverse limit is an actual functor on the derived strict-tower category, so it sends $b_K$ to an isomorphism. All maps are morphisms of $R_{T'}$-modules and thus preserve the stated $\mathcal O_E$-linear structures.

proof.text: The constructions in Steps 5--7 are natural for chain maps of flat-term K-flat representatives: tensoring, the Koszul augmentation and the balanced formulas commute with such maps. Resolving-class uniqueness identifies the calculation $GX_\bullet$ with the specified total left derived tower functor. The integral well-definedness lemma identifies $\mathsf C(B_\bullet)$ with the specified integral functor independently of resolutions. The normalized Roos map is natural on the whole derived tower category. Therefore the formula in Step 8 is natural in $K$: its naturality square holds on K-flat representatives, and descends through localization; the square for an inverted quasi-isomorphism follows by multiplying the square for that quasi-isomorphism by its inverses. This also proves independence from all representatives used in constructing $b_K$ and $\gamma_{g,K}$.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes (dual); Tag 05RU, definition-derived-category, localization descent of the explicit natural comparison.

proof.text: Denote the integral cone projection by $p_n^{\mathrm{int}}$ and the completed limit projection, followed by the evaluation of $b_K$, by $p_n^{\mathrm{comp}}$. This latter evaluation is exactly the coefficient comparison fixed in the completed-pullback definition: Steps 6--7 use its structure-map components and quotient augmentations. If $e_n:R\lim B_\bullet\to B_n$ is the limit projection, the normalized Roos lemma gives $e_n\rho_{B_\bullet}=p_n^{\mathrm{int}}$, while functoriality of limit projections gives $p_n^{\mathrm{comp}}=e_n R\lim(b_K)$. Substituting Step 8 yields $p_n^{\mathrm{comp}}\gamma_{g,K}=p_n^{\mathrm{int}}$, equivalently $p_n^{\mathrm{int}}\gamma_{g,K}^{-1}=p_n^{\mathrm{comp}}$, the requested direction. This equality follows from a strict tower comparison and the normalized Roos comparison; evaluation maps alone are not used to characterize a derived tower morphism.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, compatible projection maps in the cone/K-injective models.

proof.text: Finally check shifts on these models. With the cone coordinates $\mathsf C(B)^i=(\prod B_n)^{i-1}\oplus(\prod B_n)^i$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$, the map $\mathsf C(B[r])\to\mathsf C(B)[r]$ is $(y,x)\mapsto((-1)^r y,x)$. Substitution in the differential verifies the chain-map identity. In Step 5 use $P[r]$ for $K[r]$ and the natural shifted two-term tensor identification; Steps 6--7 commute with it, since they apply pullback, scalar multiplication and degree-zero quotient maps. For the Roos comparison choose the shifted K-injective resolution $B[r]\to I[r]$. Shifts preserve K-injectivity by its Hom-vanishing definition, and termwise limit commutes with shifts. Its normalization $z\mapsto(0,z)$ commutes with the displayed signed map. Thus $\rho_{B[r]}$ is $\rho_B[r]$ under these shift comparisons, and the same is true of $R\lim(b_K)$. The completed pullback shift of the cited triangle lemma is precisely the composite of the reduction, tower-pullback and limit shift comparisons used here. The formula of Step 8 therefore proves the asserted equality of $\gamma_{g,K[r]}$ and $\gamma_{g,K}[r]$ for every integer $r$.
